idiom_name: guard predicate + immediate return, transition inside the guard
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: give the object one state representation and one predicate that decides whether the action may run now, then evaluate the predicate and the state transition inside a single critical section (mutex, monitor or compare-and-set), returning immediately whenever the predicate is false and never blocking or enqueueing. Return an explicit outcome so the caller can distinguish refusal from success, and keep the critical section to the predicate plus the transition - nothing inside it may block, panic or call back. When callers must eventually proceed, switch to Guarded Suspension or a queue instead of making them poll.
code_sketch:
def try_start() -> bool:
    acquire_guard()              # exclusive, and non-blocking
    try:
        if not may_start(state): # predicate
            return False         # balk: no side effects
        state = RUNNING           # the single transition
        return True
    finally:
        release_guard()          # released on every path
pitfalls: Returning nothing for a balked call -> the caller cannot distinguish refusal from success and may lose work silently -> return a boolean, status, or documented exception.

Checking the predicate before taking the guard -> another caller can change the state before the transition and both calls may proceed -> evaluate the predicate and transition under one lock or compare-and-set.
Balking when the caller must eventually complete the operation -> a transient outage becomes dropped requests or busy-polling -> use Guarded Suspension, a queue, or an explicit retry owner.
Counting neither refusals nor their reason -> overload and state pressure remain invisible in production -> emit a bounded balk counter and rate by guarded operation.
Holding an async lock across an await -> unrelated tasks queue behind I/O and can deadlock through re-entrancy -> reserve the state inside the lock, release it, then await outside.

Using a process-local lock for shared state across workers or nodes -> other processes bypass the guard and admit conflicting transitions -> use an inter-process store, database constraint, or consensus primitive.
Treating a volatile or atomic dirty flag as a complete check-and-clear -> two saves can race or a new edit can be cleared -> make the compound transition atomic, then perform I/O after reserving it.

Treating a singleflight follower as a balked call -> callers that need a result see dropped cache misses even though coalescing is available -> use request coalescing when followers must share completion.
Spinning after a failed tryLock or trySend -> CPU use and starvation return while completion is still not guaranteed -> return the refusal and retry on a later event, or wait with a bounded policy.
